SIR Epidemic Model

Source: R/diffEq_models.R
model_sir.Rd

Three-compartment model with permanent immunity after recovery.

Usage

model_sir(init, params, times, ...)

Arguments

init

Named numeric vector. R defaults to 0 if omitted, e.g. c(S = 990, I = 10).

params

Named numeric vector, e.g. c(beta = 0.002, gamma = 0.1).

beta

Transmission rate.

gamma

Recovery rate (1/gamma = mean infectious period).

N

Total population size. Optional — defaults to sum(init).

b

Birth rate (per capita per time). Optional.

d

Death rate (per capita per time). Optional.

times

Numeric vector of output times.

...

Additional arguments passed to ode_solver.

Value

A data.frame with columns time, S, I, R.

Details

Closed population (default): $$\frac{dS}{dt} = -\beta \frac{S I}{N}$$ $$\frac{dI}{dt} = \beta \frac{S I}{N} - \gamma I$$ $$\frac{dR}{dt} = \gamma I$$

Open population (when b / d are provided): $$\frac{dS}{dt} = b N - \beta \frac{S I}{N} - d S$$ $$\frac{dI}{dt} = \beta \frac{S I}{N} - \gamma I - d I$$ $$\frac{dR}{dt} = \gamma I - d R$$

In the closed case population size \(N = S + I + R\) is conserved. The basic reproduction number is \(R_0 = \beta / \gamma\).

Examples

# Closed population
model_sir(
  init   = c(S = 990, I = 10),
  params = c(beta = 0.002, gamma = 0.1),
  times  = seq(0, 50, by = 0.1)
)
